note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: Brookfield plans $27 billion AI data center at power station; Drax rises 8%
items.blurb: A planned 1-gigawatt AI campus at Drax's Yorkshire power station shows the buildout chasing existing grid connections in Britain.

items.title: Blackstone president calls for more equity to fund AI buildout as debt risks mount
items.blurb: Blackstone and Pimco leaders warn lenders are growing too exposed to AI spending, which may need more equity financing.

items.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.blurb: Researchers are testing incentive design to steer AI agents without fully understanding their internals; whether agents respond predictably is unclear.

items.title: Three questions that will define AI's political power
items.blurb: Axios looks at how the Nov 3 midterm results could shape the AI industry's influence in Washington.

items.title: Palantir sinks 3% after earnings as analysts point to slowdown in total contract value
items.blurb: Revenue nearly doubled past $2 billion, but slower contract-value growth tested investor confidence in AI software spending.

items.title: CrowdStrike launches AI kill switch for rogue internal agents
items.blurb: CrowdStrike's new tool lets security teams halt misbehaving AI agents, with a Claude Cowork integration; critics question whether emergency stops work at scale.

items.title: Meta seeks to raise up to $25 billion in debt sale as AI spending jumps
items.blurb: Meta's bond sale of $20 to $25 billion would fund AI infrastructure and models, adding to a wave of debt-financed buildout.

items.title: AMD stock jumps 8% on earnings as data center revenue nearly doubles
items.blurb: AMD guided about $17 billion for the fourth quarter and expects server revenue to double in 2027 on AI chip demand.

items.title: AI-generated 'slopaganda' in political ads puts internet platforms on alert
items.blurb: Campaigns spent over $187 million on AI-made midterm ads, many without disclosures; no federal law governs them.

items.title: Google responds to political backlash over removing search from schools that ban AI
items.blurb: Google says Gemini and Search will be off by default for schools, after lawmakers called its cutoff plan extortion.

items.title: Apple stock sinks as global memory crisis hurts profits, giving Ternus his first big test
items.blurb: Apple blamed higher memory prices and some Siri AI costs for shrinking margins, as a global memory crunch squeezes hardware makers.

items.title: South Korea targets 'world's highest performance' sovereign AI model in record new budget
items.blurb: Seoul's record 2027 budget sets 4.7 trillion won for a sovereign AI model and 21.3 trillion for chips and data centers.

items.title: OpenAI deepens Abu Dhabi foothold as Sam Altman inks deals spanning energy, government and investment
items.blurb: OpenAI signed four Abu Dhabi agreements, including ADNOC and G42 deployments, while seeking up to $20 billion from UAE-led investors.

items.title: The agentic web is here
items.blurb: AI agents now browse and transact for users, threatening publisher revenue and raising fears that big platforms will wall agents in.

items.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion deal in AI data-center bet
items.blurb: The all-stock deal bets that AI spending keeps optical-component demand ahead of supply and sharpens Marvell's custom-chip fight with Broadcom.

items.title: How the 2026 midterms could affect defense, healthcare, crypto and AI stocks
items.blurb: A House-passed bill making large data centers cover grid costs stalled in the Senate; the midterms could shift those costs onto developers.

items.title: Anthropic reports $17B in Q3 revenue, purchase commitments of $895B in new S-1
items.blurb: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows revenue still surging but slowing, with nearly $900 billion committed to compute and infrastructure.

items.title: Oracle files to sell $20 billion in new stock, bonds to finance AI buildout
items.blurb: Oracle will raise $10 billion in shares and $10 billion in notes for data centers; its stock fell over 5%.

items.title: Anthropic's spending commitments surge to nearly $900 billion
items.blurb: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows about $17 billion in third-quarter revenue against nearly $900 billion in compute commitments.

items.title: Nvidia's humanoid push relies on China-made robot hands
items.blurb: Nvidia's latest humanoid robot reference platform uses hands from Chinese startup Wuji, showing supply-chain ties despite export tensions.

items.title: Apple earnings: iPhone sales lead revenue upward
items.blurb: Apple beat revenue forecasts in John Ternus's first quarter as CEO and plans to launch Apple Intelligence in China in December.

items.title: Palantir's US commercial revenue tops government sales for the first time
items.blurb: Palantir beat third-quarter estimates as corporate demand for its AI software overtook government contracts, a test of enterprise AI spending.

items.title: OpenAI hires former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for national security role
items.blurb: OpenAI created a senior counselor post to push AI into US national security and cybersecurity, and to work with allies on adoption.

items.title: Here's who is falling in line for Trump's "Super Intelligence" loyalty test
items.blurb: A September order told agencies to say "Super Intelligence" instead of AI; uneven adoption risks turning AI into a partisan issue.
